title: Trying to build a multi-agent art pipeline that copies how human artists work, where would it break?
author: zimmer550king
selftext:
I’m a solo dev starting an isometric Fallout-style CRPG. I’d rather not make one-shot generations that all look like they came from different games, so I’m trying to copy how human studios actually work. A written brief comes first, then silhouettes, then a model sheet, then each piece of clothing on its own, then assembly and a fixed lighting setup, with an orchestrator and separate agents for each role including a critic that can reject work.

For the facings I’m leaning toward building a low-poly model and rendering all directions under fixed light, the way Fallout itself did, and using a pixel tool only for props. Has anyone tried that route with generated meshes, and did the back of the character come out usable? Where would you let the agents loose and where would you keep a script instead?

I’d love to hear what failed for you before I repeat it.

comments.author: Time_Cat_5212
comments.body:
Why.  Human workflows are built for human brains, hands, and teams, whose primary mode of coordination is speaking in prose, slack messages, and vaguely implying shit.

LLMs can process 10,000 times as much text, have unlimited time, and don't have a social hierarchy or any emotions.  They also don't have resumes, portfolios, or a need to get paid.  

Most human art workflows are built to navigate social interactions and limited resources.

replies.author: caesium23
replies.body: The look of human made art is in large part a result of the workflow, and nothing in the post suggested recreating the entire social hierarchy that exists around the workflow.

comments.author: kytheon
comments.body:
You'll waste a lot of tokens on communication.

But yeah it's a good idea to have a planning phase first. Otherwise you'll be redoing a lot of assets later.

comments.author: randommmoso
comments.body:
As someone who designs ai systems for a living let me tell you nobody serious is using multi agent orchestration. 

Its all harness with skills and mcps and subs
